idiom_name: guard class with a private-by-convention resource; __getattribute__/__getattr__ interception for transparent guards
implementation_notes: Python has no enforced privacy - underscore names and name mangling ('designed mostly to avoid accidents; it still is possible to access or modify a variable that is considered private') are conventions, and vars()/object.__getattribute__ reach anything - so the pattern is hand-written as a guard class (or module facade) that owns the resource and checks the policy in every public method, with __all__ fixing the exported surface. Where the whole surface must be mediated the local idiom is an interception proxy: __getattribute__ 'is called unconditionally to implement attribute accesses', __getattr__ fills in failed lookups, and descriptors cover class-level access - but the data model documents the bypass ('This method may still be bypassed when looking up special methods as the result of implicit invocation via language syntax or built-in functions'), and the recursion-avoidance idiom itself calls object.__getattribute__. For OS resources the documented rule applies literally: os.access() before open() 'creates a security hole, because the user might exploit the short time interval between checking and opening the file' - put the decision in the single mediated operation (EAFP) and let OS permissions or a separate process carry the guarantee.
pitfalls: Name mangling is not privacy: vault._Vault__store, vars(vault), object.__getattribute__(vault, '_store') and plain attribute assignment all reach or replace the resource, so an in-process Python guard is a design convention.

__getattr__ runs only after normal lookup fails and __getattribute__ is bypassed for implicit special-method lookup, so an interception proxy can be side-stepped both by attributes that exist on the guard and by operators (len, iter, with).

The documented check-then-use hazard: os.access() before open() creates a security hole; use EAFP or the single mediated operation, and remember the permission bits themselves are set with os.chmod/stat.S_IMODE and enforced by the OS, not by the guard.
Decorator- or descriptor-based checks are bypassed when the undecorated callable is reachable, and cached decisions (lru_cache, module-level memo tables) outlive revocation.
